advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make run_mcp fail closed (or raise) when the wired in-flight gauge is missing rather than substituting a fresh always-zero gauge that makes the SIGTERM drain a silent no-op.
evidence: src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:231: `if gauge is None:`
`gauge = InFlightGauge()` then `run_http_with_grace(server, gauge)` — a fresh gauge distinct from the /health-bound one
comment admits: 'an empty gauge would silently read 0 and skip the drain'
The fresh gauge is never passed to register_health_route, so it can never increment; drain_then_exit returns immediately every time
advisory.finding: run_mcp's gauge-missing fallback creates a BRAND-NEW InFlightGauge that is not the one wired to /health, so the SIGTERM drain silently observes 0 in-flight ops forever (fails open): the check produces its 'drained' verdict identically whether the server truly idled or the gauge was never wired. It only logs a warning and proceeds rather than failing closed.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test exercising a wrapped arg-taking certified tool through FastMCP's real call/arg-validation path (not a direct fn() call), and/or apply functools.wraps to preserve the tool signature.
evidence: src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:86: `def _sync_wrapper(*args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:` — no functools.wraps, signature erased
docstring at line 82-84 claims the tool manager 'calls fn via call_fn_with_arg_validation and honours the replaced attribute' — an untested assumption
test_wrap_tool_fn_passes_args_and_kwargs_through_and_counts calls `tool.fn(...)` directly (line ~412), not through FastMCP validation
test_wired_server_moves_gauge... calls `worker = threading.Thread(target=wrapped)` — the wrapper directly, never through an MCP protocol request
advisory.finding: The `_wrap_tool_fn` replaces `tool.fn` with a generic `*args/**kwargs` closure and does not use functools.wraps; the docstring asserts FastMCP's `call_fn_with_arg_validation` 'honours the replaced attribute', but no test drives a wrapped certified tool through the real MCP/arg-validation path — every test calls the wrapped `fn` directly. If FastMCP derives or re-inspects the parameter schema from `fn`'s signature, the wrapper's opaque signature could break arg validation for real tool calls.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update the rebar-mcp --help text to reflect that the transport is now selectable (stdio or HTTP via REBAR_MCP_TRANSPORT).
evidence: src/rebar/mcp_server.py:704: `"rebar-mcp — the rebar MCP server (FastMCP, stdio transport).\n"`
src/rebar/mcp_server.py:705: `"Usage: rebar-mcp            # serve MCP over stdio (takes no options)\n"`
The diff wires run_mcp which serves HTTP when cfg.mcp.transport == 'http'
advisory.finding: main()'s --help output still describes rebar-mcp as stdio-only ('the rebar MCP server (FastMCP, stdio transport).' and 'serve MCP over stdio (takes no options)'), but this change adds a full HTTP transport driven by REBAR_MCP_TRANSPORT=http. The help text is now stale/misleading.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Install the SIGTERM handler before starting the uvicorn serving thread so no early signal escapes the bounded-grace path.
evidence: src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:211-212: `thread = threading.Thread(...)` then `thread.start()`
src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:214: `signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, make_sigterm_handler(...))` runs only afterward
Between start() and signal.signal() the default SIGTERM handler (terminate) is in effect
advisory.finding: In run_http_with_grace the SIGTERM handler is installed AFTER thread.start(); a SIGTERM delivered in the window between the serving thread starting and signal.signal() executing uses Python's default SIGTERM disposition (immediate process termination), bypassing the bounded drain entirely.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `infra/compose/opcert-ed25519-key*` and `infra/compose/mcp-static-tokens.json` to the repo-root `.dockerignore` so secrets can never enter the Docker build context / image layers.
evidence: .dockerignore lists `infra/compose/.env`, `**/.env` but no `opcert-ed25519-key` / `mcp-static-tokens.json` (.dockerignore:8-9)
Dockerfile.mcp: `COPY . /app` then `RUN uv sync ...` (context is repo root)

docker-compose.yml volumes: `./mcp-static-tokens.json:/run/secrets/mcp-static-tokens.json:ro` and `./opcert-ed25519-key:/run/secrets/opcert-ed25519-key:ro` — both live at infra/compose/ inside the build context

compose-up.sh:202 `docker compose ... up -d --build` builds from repo-root context after the materialize step; the Dockerfile.reviewbot comment notes git-ignore does NOT exclude a file from the Docker context
.gitignore:91 excludes `infra/compose/opcert-ed25519-key` from git only; `mcp-static-tokens.json` is not even listed in .gitignore
advisory.finding: Dockerfile.mcp's `COPY . /app` (build context = repo root) can bake the bind-mounted MCP secrets into an image layer: the repo-root `.dockerignore` excludes `.env`/`**/.env` but NOT `infra/compose/opcert-ed25519-key` or `infra/compose/mcp-static-tokens.json`, which the fetch-secrets/materialize slice writes next to the compose file before `docker compose up -d --build` runs.
advisory.suggested_fix: Extend .dockerignore with `infra/compose/opcert-ed25519-key`, `infra/compose/opcert-ed25519-key.*`, `infra/compose/mcp-static-tokens.json`, and `infra/compose/rebar-bot-signing-key*` (any bind-mounted secret sibling).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Run `nginx -t` before `nginx -s reload` in materialize-mcp-upstream.sh (and fail/skip the reload if validation fails).
evidence: materialize-mcp-upstream.sh: `nginx -s reload` invoked directly with no `nginx -t` gate
rebar.conf.template:48-49 warns `an upstream {} with ZERO server lines is a config error` — precisely the failure mode a validate step would catch before reload
compose-up.sh:197-199 treats the whole call as NON-FATAL (WARN only), so a bad reload is easy to miss
advisory.finding: materialize-mcp-upstream.sh runs `nginx -s reload` without a preceding `nginx -t` validation, so a reload against a config that fails validation (e.g. the seed absent/malformed, or an unrelated broken installed config) silently keeps stale workers rather than surfacing the failure.
advisory.suggested_fix: Guard the reload: `if nginx -t; then nginx -s reload; else echo 'WARN nginx -t failed; skipping reload' >&2; fi`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Constrain the MCP nginx location so only `/mcp` and `/mcp/...` match (e.g. `location = /mcp` + `location ^~ /mcp/`, or an exact/anchored form) rather than an open `/mcp` prefix.
evidence: rebar.conf.template:127 `location /mcp {` (prefix, no trailing slash) with `proxy_pass http://rebar_mcp;`
Comment at :122 states the intent is `BOTH the bare /mcp endpoint and /mcp/... match` — but nginx prefix semantics also match /mcpXYZ
advisory.finding: The nginx `location /mcp` uses a prefix match with no trailing slash, so it also matches unintended sibling paths like `/mcpfoo` or `/mcp-anything`, widening the proxied surface beyond the intended `/mcp` and `/mcp/...` endpoints.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that a certified tool raising an exception still decrements the InFlightGauge back to 0 (exercises track()'s finally).
evidence: src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:75-78 `self._increment()` / `try: yield` / `finally: self._decrement()`

Existing gauge tests (test_certified_tool_instrumentation_moves_the_gauge, test_wrap_tool_fn_passes_args_and_kwargs_through_and_counts, test_wired_server_moves_gauge...) all use a NORMALLY-RETURNING stub; none exercise a raising fn.
search of test file for `raise` shows only ConfigError/McpStartupError assertions, none for a certified-tool exception decrementing the gauge — ABSENCE.
Named violating input: a certified tool `fn` (e.g. review_plan) that raises RuntimeError mid-call — the added finally must still decrement the gauge.
advisory.finding: The InFlightGauge decrement-on-exception path is untested: no test runs a certified tool (or the track() context) that RAISES and asserts the gauge returns to 0. The track() finally-block (lines 75-78) exists precisely for this; if a wrapped certified tool raises and the gauge were to leak, the SIGTERM drain would block for the full 1200s DEFAULT_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS on every retire.
advisory.suggested_fix: In a test, wrap a certified fn that raises via instrument_certified_tools, call it under pytest.raises, and assert gauge.value == 0 afterwards.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test for run_mcp with transport='http' covering both the wired-gauge dispatch and the missing-gauge warning fallback (monkeypatching run_http_with_grace).
evidence: src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:229-243 the `if mcp_cfg.transport == "http"` branch, including the `gauge is None` fallback added in this diff.
search tests for `run_mcp` returns only test_run_mcp_stdio_delegates_to_fastmcp_run (line 591) — the http branch is never driven — ABSENCE.
Named violating input: run_mcp(server_without__rebar_in_flight_gauge, SimpleNamespace(transport="http")) — should log the warning and still start with a fresh gauge; untested.
advisory.finding: run_mcp's HTTP branch is untested — only the stdio branch has a test. The diff routes main() through run_mcp (mcp_server.py) and adds a gauge-fallback warning path (lines 231-242) for a missing gauge; neither the http dispatch to run_http_with_grace nor the missing-gauge fallback is exercised.
advisory.suggested_fix: Monkeypatch run_http_with_grace to capture its args; call run_mcp with a http config on a server both with and without _GAUGE_ATTR, asserting a gauge is always passed (fresh one when absent).

evidence: `REBAR_MCP_HTTP_HOST: "0.0.0.0"` (infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:337)
`ports:` `- "127.0.0.1:8091:8091"` (infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:357-360)
Dockerfile default also `ENV REBAR_MCP_HTTP_HOST=0.0.0.0` (infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp)
/health is intentionally unauthenticated (src/rebar/_mcp_health.py register_health_route)
advisory.finding: REBAR_MCP_HTTP_HOST is set to 0.0.0.0 (bind all interfaces) inside the container, and the /health route is served unauthenticated on that bind. Least-privilege would prefer binding only the interface the loopback host-publish targets; the 0.0.0.0 bind means any other container/network attached to this service could reach /health and /mcp directly, relying entirely on the compose port publish being loopback-only.
